item.description:
Security

  • Text in a reply can no longer become part of the conversation page. A reply, a thinking block or an image record could carry markup that the page drew as real elements, and a click on them could add an MCP server, add a permission rule or type a command into the session. The text could come from anything the agent read: a web page, a README, an issue. Replies now pass an allowlist, pictures are checked where they are read and where they are drawn, and omux only acts on a request from the page when it matches what omux itself put there. Thanks to Yusuf Karan (#73).

Added

  • A project's icon from its website. Edit Project… takes a website next to the icon: "Use Site's Icon" fetches the largest icon the site declares and keeps a copy, like a chosen picture. omux contacts only the site you typed, and only when you press the button.

Changed

  • The open tab shows only the session's name. What the session is doing moved to the tab's tooltip; the dot still shows its state.

Fixed

  • A file named by part of its path opens. A path in a reply like Store/review-notes.txt was a link that did nothing unless the file sat right under the session's folder. It is now also looked for under the project's folder, among the files the agent wrote in the conversation, and anywhere in the project; when it can't be found, the compose box says so.
  • Changing the model or effort keeps what you were writing. The chips sent their command the way a message is sent, which emptied the box.
  • ↑ brings back your last message. A slash command sent earlier, the chips' included, counted as the newest entry and came back first.
  • A stuck helper command can't freeze omux. git, gh, ssh and the agent CLIs are waited on until they exit, not until every process they left behind lets go of their output, and what runs in the background has a time limit. A commit hook or dotfile that leaves a process behind no longer freezes the window on ⌘W or stops pull request badges, diff stats and the Changes list from updating. (#66, thanks Anıl Soylu)
  • The omux command can't take the app down. A tool that hung up before its reply made the app exit, with every session in it. (#66)
  • Closing a worktree session, committing and sending images don't hold the window. The git checks before the close and commit questions, and the thumbnails of images in a prompt, are made off the main thread. (#71)
  • A file from another machine stays in its own folder here. A path with ".." in it could put the copy anywhere on this Mac. (#70)
  • Save in the file editor writes what the editor holds. Save and "Save mine" wrote the text from the last ⌘S, or nothing. (#67)
  • The conversation follows /clear. The panel stayed on the cleared conversation, or caught up only every ten seconds. (#69)
  • A Codex that restarts after updating itself stays in the background, and a slow shutdown blocks one restart, not every one after it. (#68)
  • Double-clicking the window's top strip fills the screen, or minimizes, as System Settings says. (#65)

Added

  • Home is a bento box. Its cards are tiles of different sizes on a grid: two large figures for today's prompts and tokens, the week's bars, models and projects in tiles of their own, beside the sessions that need you, the to-dos, limits and pull requests. Four columns on a wide window, two on a narrow one.
  • Tools on Home. A card lists what your agents have on this Mac: MCP servers, plugins, skills, subagents, commands and hooks, each with a count, a filter for long lists, and a switch between Claude Code's and Codex's. It shows what is set up for you, so there in every session.
  • Statistics. A page on your work with Claude Code, from the chart button on the rail or ⇧⌘Y: active time, days, sessions, tokens and commits for a month, a calendar of the last year by time or tokens, a bubble per project and session sized by its tokens, hours per day, and a log of each day's sessions with what was asked and what was committed. Click a day, a project or a session to narrow the whole page to it. Thanks to Hasan Emir Yıldırım (#61).
  • Project icons. Edit Project… takes a picture for the project; it shows on its rail tile in place of the initials. omux keeps its own small square copy, so the original can move. Thanks to Mücahit ŞEN (#62).
  • Skip permission prompts. Claude Code can start without asking before commands and edits, for every project (Settings › Sessions › "Start Claude Code in bypass permissions mode", #62) or for one (Edit Project… › "Skip permission prompts"; such a project carries a crossed shield next to its name). Both are off unless you turn them on, apply to sessions started afterwards, and leave alone a command that names its own permission mode.

Fixed

  • Claude's limits on Home. Home's card and the rail's ring each asked for the limits, and the second was turned away with "Usage unavailable"; they now share one reading.
